title: CollisionObject3D's "input_capture_on_drag" doesn't send input events if CollisionObject3D is being dragged and the mouse leaves the game window
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.stable

### System information

Linux ARM64 - Flatpak Godot 4.5.stable - Wayland & X11 - Mobile Renderer

### Issue description

When the option `input_capture_on_drag` is enabled on a `CollisionObject3D` that does not move, the signal `input_event(...)` is sent  when a mouse button is released even if the mouse leaves the game window and enters again at a different position.

However, if the `CollisionObject3D` is being dragged, the signal `input_event(...)` is no longer being sent if a mouse button is released when the mouse leaves and enters the game window at a different position.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d773c54-20bf-4246-b90d-04f58ef67f55

**What currently happens**:
No `input_event(...)` is being sent, which leaves the cube in the "pressed" state. Even if the mouse returns into the game window at a position where it is on top of the cube, this will only receive events as long as the mouse remains close enough to it.

I tried to work around this problem by adding the following code to the script:

```
func _notification(what: int) -> void:
	if what == NOTIFICATION_WM_MOUSE_ENTER:
		if !is_mouse_button_pressed:
			return
		if Input.is_mouse_button_pressed(MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT):
			# move_cube_to_mouse_position()
			pass
		else:
			_status_label.text = "Mouse Button Released"
			is_mouse_button_pressed = false
```

But it still resulted into the same behavior as if the mouse where to return to the game window right on top of the cube: The moment the mouse moves more than X pixels it stops receiving input events.


**What I would expect to happen**:
Ideally, I would prefer if  the `input_event(...)` signal will still be emitted as if the mouse hadn't left the window once the mouse enters the game window again.
Otherwise, I would like to receive a cancellation flag, so that the game can gracefully handle this situations. (perhaps the [canceled](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_inputeventmousebutton.html#class-inputeventmousebutton-property-canceled) property of `InputEventMouseButton` could be set to true?)


### Steps to reproduce

For the MRP:
1- Run the included scene.
2- Click on "Enable Cube Movement"
3- Drag & Drop the cube within the game window (this works as expected)
4- Drag the cube outside the screen and then drop it within the screen again. (this will get the cube stuck on the pressed state)

From Scratch:
0- Create a scene with a camera3D a light and an environment.
1- Copy the following script into a `MeshInstance3D` that has a `StaticBody3D` as a child. 
2- Connect the `input_event(...)` signal to the script.
3- Drag & Drop the cube within the game window (this works as expected)
4- Drag the cube outside the screen and then drop it within the screen again. (this will get the cube stuck on the pressed state)
```
extends MeshInstance3D

@export var _movement_plane: Plane = Plane(0,0,-1,5)
var is_mouse_button_pressed: bool = false

func _on_static_body_3d_input_event(camera: Node, event: InputEvent, _event_position: Vector3, _normal: Vector3, _shape_idx: int) -> void:
	if event is InputEventMouseButton:
		if is_mouse_button_pressed and event.is_released():
			is_mouse_button_pressed = false
			
		if !is_mouse_button_pressed and event.is_pressed():
			is_mouse_button_pressed = true

	if  event is InputEventMouseMotion and is_mouse_button_pressed:
		var screen_mouse_position: Vector2 = get_viewport().get_mouse_position()
		var new_global_position: Vector3 = _movement_plane.intersects_ray(camera.project_ray_origin(screen_mouse_position),camera.project_ray_normal(screen_mouse_position))
		global_position = new_global_position

```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[capture-on-drag-offscreen-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22770747/capture-on-drag-offscreen-bug.zip)
